support_query: United States Constitution ratified 1788 single union not separate confederacies
counter_query: northern confederacy more formidable than other American confederacies after 1787
note: Condition is separate confederacies. Ratification of one Constitution would show that condition was not met. Do not use the Civil War as that condition.

support_query: European colonies in North America strength relative to United States 1789-1820
counter_query: European colony attacked or seriously threatened the United States before 1820
note: Object is dangerous annoyance from nearby colonies, not later independence wars used as a proxy without the same measure.

support_query: state paper money or debt-abolition episodes versus federal episodes 1789-1860
counter_query: federal paper money rage pervading the Union
note: Do not treat Civil War greenbacks as the sentence object unless the source uses the same project.

support_query: Naval Act 1794 United States frigates
counter_query: United States navy of respectable weight in West Indies contests 1790s
note: Respectable weight if thrown into the scale of two contending parties is the object. Ship counts are not that object unless the source says so.

support_query: United States arbiter of Europe in America erelong after 1787
counter_query: United States not the arbiter of European competitions in America
note: erelong has no printed start because this file prints no collected year. Do not use a later hegemony narrative as the object.

support_query: four-year presidential term and executive firmness
counter_query: presidential firmness failed because the term was four years
note: Firmness is not a recorded series.

support_query: presidential vetoes characterized as timid rather than rash
counter_query: presidential vetoes generally rash
note: Need a series of the same characterization, not one veto.

support_query: presidents failed to veto when necessary more often than they vetoed too often
counter_query: presidents used the veto too often
note: Same measure problem.

support_query: presidents wisdom and integrity in treaties
counter_query: a president whose treaty concurrence was not desirable for wisdom or integrity
note: Always bid fair is not a headcount of virtue.

support_query: presidents of at least respectable abilities
counter_query: a president lacking respectable abilities
note: No closed measure of respectable abilities.

support_query: judiciary least dangerous department to constitutional rights
counter_query: judiciary more dangerous than legislature or executive to constitutional rights
note: Least dangerous is comparative and needs the same object, not one decision.

support_query: judiciary successfully attacked legislature or executive by force
counter_query: judiciary did not successfully attack the other departments
note: Voiding a statute is the design he defends, not the attack he denies.

support_query: general liberty endangered by courts while judiciary remained distinct
counter_query: general liberty not endangered from the courts
note: Conditional on remaining truly distinct. One case is not the general liberty.

support_query: state courts retained pre-1789 jurisdiction except enumerated exclusive grants
counter_query: state courts lost jurisdiction that was not exclusively delegated
note: Need the same jurisdictional object.

support_query: state courts took cognizance of federal causes unless Congress excluded them
counter_query: Congress or courts denied state cognizance of federal causes that were not expressly excluded
note: Do not substitute diversity jurisdiction doctrine for this sentence.

support_query: state civil and criminal jury continued after the Constitution
counter_query: Constitution abolished jury trial in a class of cases
note: Seventh Amendment is not abolition.

support_query: extent of change in state jury practice caused by the Constitution
counter_query: jury institution affected to a great extent by the Constitution
note: Great extent needs a before-after measure.

support_query: state constitutions kept civil jury for ordinary cases
counter_query: civil jury in ordinary state cases was altered by the federal plan
note: Full force and untouched is stronger than mere survival.

support_query: Constitution prohibition of titles of nobility remained
counter_query: United States granted titles of nobility
note: The consequence is serious danger that the government will be other than that of the people. A title prohibition is the condition, not the consequence.

support_query: citizens better informed about members of Congress than about state legislators through state governments
counter_query: citizens less informed about national representatives than about state representatives
note: No same-object information series is assumed.

support_query: Tariff or Collection Act 1789 federal officers collected import duties and states did not
counter_query: states continued to collect import duties after 1789
note: Object is collection of duties, not later income or sales taxes.

support_query: number and pay of federal customs officers versus prior state customs officers
counter_query: federal customs establishment larger or higher paid than the state establishments it replaced
note: Need the same pre-Constitution state baseline.

support_query: cost of federal judges relative to federal expenditure in the early republic
counter_query: judicial support was a material object of federal expense
note: Material consequence is undefined.

support_query: length of early Congress sessions versus Confederation Congress
counter_query: early Congress sat constantly and spending rose by that cause
note: Saving until the House greatly increased. A modern budget is not the object.

support_query: number of persons in Congress versus one fourth of state legislators circa 1788
counter_query: Congress exceeded one fourth or one fifth of the 1788 state-legislator total
note: The text says two thousand and upwards, so the base has no upper bound.

support_query: length of state legislative sessions before and after 1789
counter_query: state legislatures sat as long or longer after federal business was removed
note: Heretofore is the Confederation period, not a modern session calendar.

support_query: amendments adopted after ratification versus amendments required before ratification
counter_query: a prior amendment of the whole plan was required and obtained before the Constitution operated
note: Thirteen-to-nine is his probability argument, not an observed frequency by itself.

support_query: occasions when nine or ten states united in desiring one amendment
counter_query: an amendment desired by ten states that did not take place
note: United in the desire is the condition. A failed amendment without that showing is not the object.

support_query: text of amendments ratified in 1791 that limit powers rather than only organization
counter_query: amendments that only reorganized offices
note: Any useful amendment will not concern the mass of powers. A ratified power-limiting amendment is a counterexample only if the archived body states both the text and a full event date.

support_query: Congress obliged to call a convention when two thirds of the states apply
counter_query: Congress had an option and declined a qualifying application
note: Nine states concurring must be the application named in the sentence, not a modern count of unrelated applications.

support_query: press clauses and whether they increased security against taxation of publications
counter_query: a press declaration prevented a tax that would have been valid without it
note: The printed sentence is syntactically broken and is not repaired.

support_query: wars between separate American states producing extensive military establishments
counter_query: United States military used as if it were the disunion conditional
note: Disunion did not occur. The Civil War is not wars between states in a disunited situation.
